items.title: Getting Started with Browser Extension Development
items.content_html:
Getting Started with Browser Extension Development

Browser extensions are powerful tools that can enhance user productivity and provide custom functionality. In this tutorial, we’ll walk through creating your first browser extension that works across Chrome, Firefox, and Edge.

What You’ll Learn

  • Setting up your development environment
  • Understanding manifest files
  • Creating popup interfaces
  • Working with content scripts
  • Publishing to browser stores

Prerequisites

Before we begin, make sure you have:

  • Basic knowledge of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
  • A code editor (VS Code recommended)
  • Chrome, Firefox, or Edge browser for testing

Step 1: Project Setup

Create a new folder for your extension:

mkdir my-first-extension
cd my-first-extension

Every browser extension starts with a manifest.json file that describes your extension:

{
  "manifest_version": 3,
  "name": "My First Extension",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "A simple extension tutorial",
  "permissions": ["activeTab"],
  "action": {
    "default_popup": "popup.html",
    "default_icon": {
      "16": "icons/icon16.png",
      "48": "icons/icon48.png",
      "128": "icons/icon128.png"
    }
  }
}

Step 2: Creating the Popup

Create a popup.html file:

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <style>
      body {
        width: 300px;
        padding: 20px;
        font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
      }
      button {
        background: #007cba;
        color: white;
        border: none;
        padding: 10px 20px;
        border-radius: 5px;
        cursor: pointer;
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <h2>CodEnity Extension</h2>
    <p>Welcome to your first browser extension!</p>
    <button id="clickButton">Click Me!</button>
    <script src="popup.js"></script>
  </body>
</html>

Step 3: Adding Functionality

Create popup.js:

document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  const button = document.getElementById("clickButton");

  button.addEventListener("click", function () {
    // Get current tab
    chrome.tabs.query({ active: true, currentWindow: true }, function (tabs) {
      // Send message to content script
      chrome.tabs.sendMessage(tabs[0].id, {
        action: "highlight",
        message: "Hello from CodEnity Extension!",
      });
    });
  });
});

Cross-Browser Compatibility

To make your extension work across browsers, use the WebExtension API standard:

For Firefox (manifest.json additions):

{
  "browser_specific_settings": {
    "gecko": {
      "id": "your-extension@codenity.com",
      "strict_min_version": "91.0"
    }
  }
}

For Edge:

Edge uses the same Manifest V3 format as Chrome, making porting straightforward.

Testing Your Extension

  1. Chrome: Go to chrome://extensions/, enable Developer mode, click “Load unpacked”
  2. Firefox: Go to about:debugging, click “This Firefox”, click “Load Temporary Add-on”
  3. Edge: Go to edge://extensions/, enable Developer mode, click “Load unpacked”

Publishing to Stores

Once your extension is ready:

  1. Chrome Web Store: Requires $5 developer fee, review process ~1-3 days
  2. Mozilla Add-ons: Free, review process ~1-7 days
  3. Edge Add-ons: Free, review process ~1-7 days

Best Practices

  • Security: Never inject untrusted content
  • Performance: Minimize background scripts
  • Privacy: Be transparent about data usage
  • UX: Keep interfaces simple and intuitive

Resources

  • Chrome Extension Documentation
  • Firefox Extension Documentation
  • CodEnity Extension Examples

Next Steps

In our next tutorial, we’ll cover:

  • Advanced content script techniques
  • Working with browser APIs
  • Extension security best practices
  • Automated testing strategies

Found this tutorial helpful? Check out our other development guides and don’t forget to subscribe to our YouTube channel for video tutorials!
items.summary: Learn how to create powerful browser extensions from scratch with our step-by-step tutorial covering all major browsers.

items.title: The Researcher Extension: New Features & Updates
items.content_html:
The Researcher Extension: New Features & Updates

We’re excited to announce a major update to The Researcher extension! This release brings powerful new features designed to supercharge your research workflow across Chrome, Firefox, and Edge browsers.

🎉 What’s New in v2.1.0

Enhanced Search Intelligence

  • AI-Powered Suggestions: Get smarter search recommendations based on your research context
  • Cross-Reference Detection: Automatically identify related topics and sources
  • Search History Analytics: Understand your research patterns with detailed insights

Improved Note-Taking

  • Rich Text Editor: Format your research notes with full styling support
  • Auto-Save: Never lose your research with intelligent auto-saving
  • Tag System: Organize findings with customizable tags and categories

Performance Optimizations

  • 50% Faster Loading: Streamlined codebase for lightning-quick responses
  • Reduced Memory Usage: More efficient resource management
  • Better Mobile Support: Enhanced experience on mobile browsers

📊 User-Requested Features

Based on your feedback, we’ve added:

Quick Actions Panel

// New shortcut commands
Ctrl+Shift+R - Quick research mode
Ctrl+Shift+N - Create new note
Ctrl+Shift+S - Save current session

Export Options

  • Export research sessions as PDF
  • Markdown export for documentation
  • JSON format for data processing
  • Direct integration with popular note-taking apps

🔧 Technical Improvements

Cross-Browser Compatibility

We’ve improved compatibility across all major browsers:

Feature Chrome Firefox Edge
Core Functionality ✅ ✅ ✅
AI Suggestions ✅ ✅ ✅
Export Options ✅ ✅ ✅
Sync Support ✅ ✅ ✅

Security Enhancements

  • End-to-End Encryption: All research data is encrypted locally
  • Privacy-First: No tracking, no data collection
  • Secure Sync: Optional encrypted cloud sync for your devices

🚀 Installation & Updates

New Users

Get The Researcher extension from your browser’s official store:

  • Chrome Web Store
  • Mozilla Add-ons
  • Edge Add-ons

Existing Users

The update will be automatically pushed to all users over the next 24-48 hours. You can also manually check for updates in your browser’s extension settings.

💡 Tips for Maximum Productivity

Research Workflow Optimization

  1. Use Keyboard Shortcuts: Master the quick actions for faster navigation
  2. Organize with Tags: Create a consistent tagging system for your research
  3. Export Regularly: Keep backups of important research sessions
  4. Sync Across Devices: Enable sync to access your research anywhere

Advanced Features

# Research Session Template

## Objective: [Your research goal]

## Sources: [Primary sources list]

## Key Findings: [Main discoveries]

## Next Steps: [Action items]

## References: [Citations and links]

🗺️ Roadmap: What’s Next?

Planned for Q2 2026

  • Team Collaboration: Share research sessions with team members
  • API Integration: Connect with academic databases and research tools
  • Voice Notes: Add voice memo functionality
  • Mobile App: Dedicated mobile application

Community Requests

We’re actively working on:

  • Integration with Notion, Obsidian, and other note-taking tools
  • Advanced citation management
  • Research timeline visualization
  • Custom themes and layouts

🐛 Bug Fixes

This release addresses several user-reported issues:

  • Fixed search results not loading on some websites
  • Resolved sync conflicts when using multiple devices
  • Improved extension startup time
  • Fixed dark mode compatibility issues
  • Enhanced keyboard navigation accessibility

📈 Performance Metrics

Our testing shows significant improvements:

  • Loading Time: Reduced from 3.2s to 1.6s average
  • Memory Usage: Down 35% compared to v2.0
  • Crash Rate: Reduced by 90%
  • User Satisfaction: 4.8/5 stars across all platforms

🙋‍♀️ Need Help?

Support Resources

  • Documentation: Comprehensive user guide
  • Video Tutorials: Step-by-step video guides
  • Contact Support: Get personalized help
  • Community Forum: Connect with other researchers

Feedback Welcome

We love hearing from our users! Share your thoughts:

  • Rate us on your browser’s extension store
  • Join our beta program for early access to new features
  • Follow us for updates and tips

🎬 Watch the Demo

Check out our latest video showcasing the new features:

Video tutorial coming soon on our YouTube channel!

Ready to supercharge your research? Download The Researcher extension today and experience the power of intelligent research assistance!

Stay tuned for more updates and don’t forget to subscribe to our newsletter for the latest CodEnity news.

items.title: Introduction to CodEnity Blog - Welcome to Our Development Journey
items.content_html:
Welcome to the official CodEnity Blog! We’re excited to launch this platform where we’ll share insights, tutorials, updates, and our development journey as we work to bridge the gap between code and craft.

Who We Are

CodEnity is a team passionate about creating tools that enhance the developer experience. From browser extensions that boost productivity to educational content that helps developers grow their skills, we’re committed to building solutions that matter to the coding community.

What You Can Expect

Our blog will cover a wide range of topics:

🚀 Product Updates & Announcements

  • New features and improvements to our browser extensions
  • Release notes and changelogs
  • Beta testing opportunities for the community

💻 Technical Tutorials

  • Step-by-step guides on browser extension development
  • Web development best practices
  • Code optimization techniques
  • Tool recommendations and reviews

🎯 Industry Insights

  • Trends in web development
  • Analysis of new technologies and frameworks
  • Developer productivity tips
  • Open source project highlights

🛠️ Behind the Scenes

  • Our development process and methodologies
  • Challenges we face and how we solve them
  • Tool stack decisions and architecture choices
  • Lessons learned from our projects

Our Current Projects

We’re currently focused on several key projects:

  1. CodEditor Extension: A powerful code editing tool for browsers
  2. CodHelper Extension: Productivity utilities for developers
  3. Educational Content: Tutorials and guides on our YouTube channel
  4. Open Source Contributions: Contributing back to the developer community

Join Our Community

We believe in building in public and sharing our knowledge with the community. Here’s how you can connect with us:

  • Subscribe to our blog: Get notified about new posts and updates
  • Follow us on YouTube: @codenity-iki for video tutorials and demos
  • Try our extensions: Available on Chrome Web Store and other browsers
  • Engage with our content: Leave comments, share your thoughts, and suggest topics

What’s Coming Next

In the coming weeks, you can expect:

  • Detailed tutorials on building browser extensions from scratch
  • Analysis of popular JavaScript frameworks for extension development
  • Performance optimization techniques for web applications
  • Case studies from our own development experiences

Feedback and Suggestions

This blog is for the developer community, and we want to create content that truly helps. If you have:

  • Topic suggestions
  • Questions you’d like us to address
  • Feedback on our content or tools
  • Collaboration opportunities

Please don’t hesitate to reach out! We read every comment and email.

Stay Updated

To never miss an update:

  1. Subscribe to our RSS feed at /feed.xml
  2. Bookmark our blog at /blog/
  3. Follow our social channels for quick updates

Thank you for joining us on this journey. We’re excited to share what we’re building and learning, and we hope our content helps you on your own development path.

Happy coding! 🚀

The CodEnity Team

P.S. This blog is built with Jekyll and hosted on GitHub Pages. We’ll be sharing the technical details of how we built this platform in an upcoming post. Stay tuned!
